query: Arm smartphone royalty revenue mobile chips
normalized: arm chips mobile revenue royalty smartphone

output.content:
**Arm’s smartphone/mobile-chip royalty revenue:** Arm does not publicly disclose a dollar amount for smartphone royalties, but smartphones remain a major royalty contributor and are benefiting from higher-value chips rather than unit-market growth alone. [[1]]

- In **Q1 FY2026** (quarter ended June 2025), total royalty revenue was **$585 million**, up **25% year over year**; management said smartphone royalties grew “an order of magnitude faster than the market,” driven by flagship phones using Armv9 and Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS). [[2]]
- In **Q2 FY2026** (quarter ended September 2025), royalties reached **$620 million**, up **21% YoY**, with growth across smartphones, data center, automotive and IoT. [[3]]
- In **Q3 FY2026** (quarter ended December 2025), royalties were **$737 million**, up **27% YoY**; Arm cited smartphones among the growth end markets, while emphasizing Armv9/CSS and data-center chip usage as major drivers of higher royalty rates. [[4]]
- In **Q4 FY2026** (quarter ended March 2026), royalties were **$671 million**, up **11% YoY**; Arm again attributed the increase to Armv9, CSS and greater data-center use. [[5]] 

The key economic point is that Arm earns royalties when licensees ship chips containing Arm designs, so royalty revenue is driven by both chip shipments and royalty rate/product mix. [[6]] Arm’s current mobile opportunity is therefore less about smartphone unit growth and more about monetization per premium handset chip: Armv9 carries a higher per-chip royalty than earlier architectures, and CSS raises Arm’s royalty revenue per chip by supplying more of the chip design. [[7]] 

For context, Arm says its energy-efficient CPUs were present in **more than 99% of smartphones sold in FY2026**, illustrating the scale of the mobile installed base from which royalties can be generated. [[8]] However, Arm is deliberately diversifying: its FY2026 royalty growth was also supported by cloud/data center, automotive and IoT, so it would be incorrect to treat consolidated royalty growth as smartphone-only. [[3]] [[4]]
